# Christina Cacioppo’s Post

 

 Christina Cacioppo 

Today, we’re announcing Vanta's Series D and new valuation: $4.15 billion. Vanta’s mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We started by automating SOC 2 for startups. Our first product helped startups compete on a level playing field and build trust faster. Before Vanta, “you can’t automate a SOC 2.” Then, as we’d hoped, the world began to move past annual, check-the-box audits. The bar to demonstrate trust ratcheted up, and we responded by building Trust Centers and products for vendor risk, access reviews, and risk management. We want to shift security reviews from static, point-in-time checks to continuous, automated verification. I’m a fan of the parable about “the back of the chessboard,” which explains the power of compounding. If Vanta’s taught me anything, it’s to be in awe of compounding. It feels like we’re stacking the chessboard at Vanta: * 200M+ assets continuously monitored from laptops to servers to employees * 1.5M employees and 33,000 vendors managed to reduce access risk and secure third-party relationships * 1.7B vulnerabilities remediated within SLA, keeping customers ahead * 10M Trust Center views, each one a potential purchase made faster with automated, self-serve

Today we're launching Computer Use for the Vanta Agent. Of the 650,000 images uploaded to Vanta in the past six months, 36% were screenshots because evidence and control monitoring outside an API required as much. The Vanta Agent can now use a computer to capture screenshots with scoped access, one-click approval, and a full record of every artifact created.

Screenshot evidence collection has been one of our biggest requests, and we couldn't have built it until recently. The last couple of months have been all about finding the jagged edge of AI capabilities and translating it to our customers.

**Christina Cacioppo**: Cofounder and CEO at Vanta for 9 years 2 months with 9 years 3 months of total professional experience. Based in San Francisco, California, United States [US].

---

Thrilled to announce we’ve raised $150mm Series C at a $2.45bn post valuation led by Sequoia Capital alongside all our existing investors – Y Combinator, CrowdStrike, Atlassian, HubSpot, Workday, and Craft Ventures – and new investors Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan. The terms on this round are exactly as we aim Vanta experiences to be: straightforward and clean.

I couldn’t be more proud of how we’ve put customers first since the Series B two years ago. That daily work shows up in this round and in our output metrics: Vanta now has over 8000 customers, almost 2x as many as last year – we’re adding customers faster than ever before; our customer growth outside of the US is faster than inside; and Trust Management is starting to catch on.

We didn’t need to raise this round – we had ⅔ of the Series B in the bank – but we chose to in order to better serve our customers:

🤖 We’re building AI and LLM-enabled features for our customers first, not for ourselves. Questionnaire Automation is actually really good – 80-90% answer approvals!

I started Vanta after working on Dropbox Paper and seeing how impossible it was for us to reach enterprises without documented security and compliance practices. We'd have early usage, customers would love the product, but then we couldn't move forward because we hadn't built and earned trust with enterprise procurement.

The whole compliance process seemed stuck in the 1990s when viewed from the outside: expensive consultants, months of work, and treating IT attestations like a once-a-year checkbox instead of something continuous. I kept thinking: we're a tech company, why can't we automate this?

So in 2018, I built Vanta to do exactly that. We automated the tedious parts of compliance and help all companies build and earn trust, not just enterprises with huge budgets.

That context and background makes this video especially fun. We tried to emulate the best of HBO's Silicon Valley and there's a few easter eggs in the video and campaign page. Let me know if you spot them?

Proud to announce that Vanta has been selected to serve on the Federal Secure Cloud Advisory Committee (FSCAC), one of only two large businesses represented on the 15-person committee, which spans both the government and industry participants.

Serving on the FSCAC is a responsibility that we are honored to take on. The FSCAC advises the GSA, FedRAMP® Board, and federal agencies on how to securely adopt cloud products and services, as well as examines how FedRAMP operates, gathers feedback on how agencies implement its requirements, and serves as a forum for the broader FedRAMP community.

I’d also like to congratulate Zack Fasnacht, our Public Sector Product Manager, who will represent Vanta and the broader industry perspective on the Committee. Before Vanta, Zack worked within the Risk Management Framework at both the U.S. Department of Homeland Security and the Library of Congress, including leading the development of DHSChat.

It's not lost on us what this seat represents, and we value the trust that comes with it. Vanta has gone through FedRAMP ourselves and we have helped others achieve their own FedRAMP certification, giving us a first-hand understanding of what it takes to deliver and adopt cloud technology securely.
